title: Converting a public trust into a Section 8 company
law: Sections 366 and 374 and Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013; Companies (Authorised to Register) Rules, 2014
summary: Registers an existing public trust as a Section 8 (not-for-profit) company limited by guarantee, with a fresh certificate and licence from the Registrar.
when: When the trustees want to run the charitable activity through a company instead of a trust.
applies: Registered public trusts (Maharashtra Public Trusts Act, 1950 in the reference note); proposed company is a Section 8 company limited by guarantee

steps.d: Confirm the trust is a registered public trust and its registration and deed changes are current. Check tax, Charity Commissioner and other compliances, licences (school, hospital etc.), NOCs from authorities and secured lenders, that the objects fit Section 8, accounts are current, and proposed directors hold active DINs and are not disqualified.
The trustees meet and approve the conversion into a Section 8 company and the application to the Central Registration Centre for a name.

File SPICe+ Part A with a signed explanatory letter, a certified copy of the resolution and the trust registration certificate. Approval lasts a short time, so extend it to the maximum allowed because the whole process takes at least 30 to 45 days.

After name approval, the trustees note the name and approve the draft MOA and AOA, the first directors and members, the list of secured creditors and the plan for NOCs. They also settle the newspaper notice, the letters to the authorities and the date for the financial statements.

Publish notice in Form URC-2, in English and a local-language paper, in the district of the trust's registered office, inviting objections (Section 374(b), Rule 4). The application must be filed within 30 days of publication, so plan dates backwards.
Send a copy of the published notice to the Charity Commissioner, the Income Tax authority and the Central Registration Centre, asking for objections, if any.
Wait out the 21 days. Prepare financial statements with notes, not older than 15 days on the application date, and have the auditor certify them.
steps.time: Not older than 15 days at filing

steps.d: Prepare the declarations, affidavits, consents and statements listed in the checklist, including the statement of work, assets and liabilities, three-year income and expenditure projection, and the affidavit of the authorised representative.
File SPICe+ Part B with INC-9, AGILE-PRO-S, the e-MOA and e-AOA and URC-1, with the attachments. File within the period allowed from name approval or the extended period.
steps.time: Within the validity of the reserved name

steps.d: The Registrar checks the forms and may ask for more or fewer documents or other changes.
On satisfaction, the Registrar issues a fresh Certificate of Incorporation and the Section 8 licence.
Send the Charity Commissioner an intimation of the registration with the supporting set of trust and filing documents.
After conversion, no application to convert into any other kind of company can be made for ten years from incorporation, except private to public or public to private.

The reference note says the name reservation is valid for 20 days and can be extended to 60. Verify the current validity rules on the portal.

title: Converting a Section 8 company into a private limited company
law: Section 8(4); Rules 21, 22 and 23 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014
summary: Moves a not-for-profit Section 8 company out of that status into an ordinary private limited company, with approval of the Regional Director.
when: When a Section 8 company wants to stop being a not-for-profit company.

steps.d: Confirm all financial statements and annual returns are filed, and if the application falls more than three months after the last year end, prepare a CA-certified financial position not older than 30 days. Check directors are not disqualified and DINs and DSCs are active. Decide if main objects change. Check concessions, grants, land and donations received, lender and authority NOCs.
Approve the conversion, the altered MOA and AOA for a private company, and fix the date, time and venue of the EGM with its notice.
Pass a special resolution to convert, and ordinary resolutions to note the altered MOA and AOA.
File the special resolution with the Registrar.
Publish Form INC-19 at least once in a local-language paper and once in an English paper widely read in the district, and on the company website if it has one.

Send the notice with the application and attachments by registered post or by hand to the Chief Commissioner of Income Tax, the Income Tax Officer, the Charity Commissioner, the Chief Secretary of the State and any other authority that oversees the company. They may make representations to the Regional Director.

File INC-18 with INC-33 and INC-34, with the attachments listed in the checklist: resolution, EGM notice, proposed MOA and AOA, financials, CA and professional certificates, newspaper notice, NOCs and directors' declarations.
docs: Certificate of incorporation, PAN and Section 8 licence

steps.d: File GNL-2 with a copy of the INC-18 application and annexures.
The Regional Director may ask for approvals from other authorities and may call for the Registrar's report. If satisfied, the Director issues an order approving conversion on any conditions needed.
File the Regional Director's order with the Registrar.
After the order, adopt the private-company MOA and AOA in the Schedule I model forms, and fix the EGM and its notice.
Pass special resolutions to adopt the new MOA and AOA.
File the special resolutions adopted at the second EGM.
File INC-20 with INC-33 and INC-34 and a certified copy of the order, plus a directors' declaration that all conditions have been met.
steps.time: Within 30 days of receiving the order

steps.d: The Registrar registers the documents and issues a fresh Certificate of Incorporation.
Check whether INC-20A (declaration for commencement of business) applies for subscription of shares of the private company.

title: Issuing unsecured compulsorily convertible debentures (private company)
law: Section 71 and Rule 18 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014; Section 62 and Rule 13 of the same Rules; Section 42 and Rule 14 of the Companies (Prospectus and Allotment of Securities) Rules, 2014
summary: Raises money by issuing unsecured debentures that must be converted into shares, offered privately to chosen persons.
when: When a private company wants to raise funds from identified investors through compulsorily convertible debentures.

steps.d: Obtain a valuation report on the debentures from a registered valuer. Make sure the valuer's registration number is on the report.
Approve the issue of debentures, identify the persons to be offered, approve the offer letter in Form PAS-4 and approve the EGM notice, explanatory statement and meeting details.
File MGT-14 for the board resolution approving the issue.
steps.time: Within 30 days of the board resolution

steps.d: Pass a special resolution for the issue of convertible debentures on a preferential basis. Allotment under it must be completed within twelve months of passing it.
File MGT-14 for the special resolution.
Open a separate account with a scheduled bank to receive the subscription money.
List the people to whom the offer will go. The offer letter can go out only after MGT-14 is filed.
Dispatch the PAS-4 letter of offer to the chosen persons and record those who received it in Form PAS-5.
Accept application money only by cheque, demand draft or other banking channel, never cash. Keep a record of the bank accounts from which payments came.
Allot the debentures and approve the debenture certificates, to be signed by two directors and the company secretary, if any. Pay stamp duty on the value allotted.
File Form PAS-3.

If debentures go to foreign persons or entities, get the FIRC and KYC from the company's authorised dealer bank, attach the valuation report (by a CA or merchant banker as per FEMA rules), and obtain other certificates and declarations. Create entity and business users on the RBI FIRMS portal if not done.
File FC-GPR on the RBI FIRMS portal. FEMA says 'issue'; read it as allotment.

title: Nomination by a security holder
law: Section 72 of the Companies Act, 2013; Rule 19 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014; Rule 3 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014 (for One Person Companies)
summary: Lets a holder of shares or debentures name a person who takes the securities on the holder's death, and to change or cancel the nomination later.
when: When a shareholder or debenture holder wants a nominee, or wants to change or cancel one; or on incorporating an OPC.
applies: All companies; special route for OPCs and for demat holdings

steps.d: A sole holder, or all joint holders together, apply to the company in Form SH-13 with the nominee's consent, PAN and address proof.
docs: Nominee consent, PAN and address proof

steps.d: For an OPC, nominee details go in Form INC-3 with the nominee's consent, PAN and address proof at the time of incorporation. Nomination is part of incorporation itself.
The company checks the form and papers and, if in order, records the nomination and enters it at once in the register of members kept under Section 88 in Form MGT-1.
The Registrar examines the incorporation papers and issues the certificate. The OPC then notes the nomination in its register of members.
The holder gives notice of cancellation or change of nominee to the company in Form SH-14. It takes effect on the day the company receives it.
The member gives notice to the company of the intended change. The new nominee's details go in INC-3 with consent, PAN and address proof, and are filed with the Registrar in Form INC-4.
If the nominee is a minor, the holder may name another person, in the prescribed form, to take the securities if the nominee dies while a minor.
For demat shares, the depository participant gives clients nomination forms, usually during KYC updates, and passes the updated list to the registrar and transfer agent.

The nominee gives written notice with the death certificate and elects to be registered as holder or to transfer the securities. Transfer rules apply as if the holder were alive. Until registered, the nominee gets dividends and benefits but cannot exercise membership rights at meetings. The Board may require an election; if none within 90 days, it may hold back dividends and other money.

flags: The reference note says Rule 19(11) uses SH-14 and SH-13 together; garbled in the reference note. Verify which form the holder uses to appoint a person for a minor nominee.

The reference note reproduces Rule 3(5) twice with different content. Rule 3 says a Section 8 conversion is not possible for an OPC and that an OPC cannot do NBFC or investment activity. Verify against the current rule text.
The reference note says INC-3 details are 'filed in INC-4' on change. Check whether INC-3 is attached to INC-4 on the portal.
For listed companies, SEBI has prescribed its own nomination forms and rules for demat and physical holdings. The reference note does not cover these; verify.

title: Applying for extension of time to hold the AGM
law: Sections 96, 117(3) and 179(3)(d); Rule 12 of the Companies (Registration Offices and Fees) Rules, 2014; Rule 24 of the Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014; SEBI LODR Regulations 30, 34, 36, 44, 46 and 47
summary: Asks the Registrar for up to three more months to hold an AGM that cannot be held on time.
when: When the AGM cannot be held within six months of year end (or within 15 months of the last AGM) because of real delays.
applies: All companies except OPC; SEBI steps for listed companies only

steps.d: When delays in accounts, audit, approvals, disputes, system changes or other events make the AGM date unreachable, the responsible officer tells the Board or the compliance head at once.
Send notice to all directors at their registered address or email. The reference note asks for at least 7 days before the AGM date. Shorter notice is acceptable if the directors ratify it.

Check quorum, place the item, discuss why the AGM cannot be held in time, approve the request to the Registrar and authorise a director or company secretary to file GNL-1 and MGT-14 with the resolution.
Delay in accounts may be unpublished price sensitive information. Record it in the structured digital database with the date, time and names of persons it was shared with.
Disclose the board's decision to the stock exchanges under Regulation 30.
Show the change on the company website under Regulation 46(2)(b).

The authorised officer prepares GNL-1 and MGT-14, stating the reasons and the period asked for. Attach the certified board resolution, a letter on the company letterhead, and supporting papers such as auditor's communication or restructuring documents.
File GNL-1 and MGT-14 online under Rule 12 with the prescribed fee.
The Registrar reviews the papers and may seek clarifications or more evidence. Reply quickly and accurately.

If satisfied, the Registrar allows an extension of up to three months beyond the due date. If not, the Registrar rejects or asks for more information; resubmit with clarifications. Missing the deadline can lead to penalties.
Disclose the extension and the revised AGM schedule to the exchanges and shareholders under Regulations 30 and 34, and post the order on the website.

After approval, hold a board meeting to fix the AGM date, time and venue, approve the notice, reports, e-voting agency and scrutiniser. Send the notice and annual report, and publish the newspaper summary if listed. Hold the AGM within the extension.

docs.title: Application letter to the Registrar
paras: To, The Registrar of Companies, [city]. Subject: Application under Section 96(1) for extension of time to hold the Annual General Meeting of {co}, CIN [CIN], for the year ended [date].
The company could not hold its AGM by [due date] because [reasons]. The Board approved this application at its meeting on [date]. We request an extension of [period] up to [date].
We enclose the certified board resolution and [supporting documents]. Yours faithfully, [name], [designation], for {co}.

flags: The reference note asks for board notice 'at least 7 days before the AGM date'. Section 173(3) requires 7 days before the board meeting itself. Use the board meeting date.

The reference note files MGT-14 for the board resolution. A board resolution to apply for an AGM extension is not obviously in Section 117(3) or Rule 24; check whether MGT-14 is needed. GNL-1 is the main application.

The Registrar can extend only an AGM other than the first one, by up to three months, for a special reason (Section 96(1) third proviso). Apply before the deadline expires. The reference note does not say this clearly.
Treating AGM delay as UPSI for the SDD is the reference note's view; verify with your insider trading policy.
Deadlines for MGT-7, AOC-4 and ADT-1 are not in the reference note; they follow the Act (generally 60 days, 30 days and 15 days).
private: Steps that apply only to listed companies and do not apply to private companies, in the reference note's numbering: 4 (entries in the structured digital database), 5 (Board outcome disclosure under Regulation 30), 6 (website update on AGM details), 11 (intimation to the stock exchange) and 12 (putting the order on the website). They come from Regulations 30, 34, 36, 44, 46 and 47 of the Listing Regulations.

title: Getting a digital signature certificate for MCA filings
law: Rule 8(4) of the Companies (Registration Offices and Fees) Rules, 2014; Section 398 of the Companies Act, 2013
summary: Gets a Class 3 digital signature certificate from a licensed authority and registers it on the MCA portal.
when: Before anyone signs and files MCA e-forms.
applies: All companies and LLPs; no relaxation for private companies

steps.d: Pick a certifying authority licensed by the Controller of Certifying Authorities. Examples are eMudhra, NSDL, Safescrypt, Capricorn and Verasys. The CCA website lists all.

Fill in the application online or offline on the authority's portal. Pick validity of 1 to 3 years, Class 3 for MCA filings, and sign or sign-and-encrypt. Give personal and organisation details if needed.

Individuals give PAN, address proof, Aadhaar or e-KYC, and a photo. For a DSC on behalf of a company or LLP, also give the certificate of incorporation, PAN, address proof, GST certificate and a board resolution or authorisation letter, plus the signatory's own papers.
Complete Aadhaar-based e-KYC and a video verification. Keep original identity and address proofs ready.
Pay the authority's fee, which depends on validity and type.
After verification the authority issues the DSC, as a soft download or on a secure USB token.
Log in, choose Register DSC, install the MCA emSigner utility and map the DSC.
Sign and submit MCA e-forms, tender documents and other statutory filings.

checklist: PAN card
Address proof
Aadhaar for e-KYC
Passport-size photo
Company papers and authorisation letter if for a company
Class 3 certificate chosen, validity chosen
Fee paid
emSigner installed and DSC registered on MCA portal
Renewal date noted

docs.title: Authorisation letter for a company DSC
paras: To, [name of certifying authority]. We, {co}, CIN [CIN], authorise [name of signatory], [designation], PAN [PAN], to apply for and hold a Class 3 digital signature certificate for signing documents filed with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs on behalf of the company.
This authorisation was given by the Board at its meeting held on [date]. For {co}, [name of director], DIN [DIN].

flags: The list of licensed authorities in the reference note should be checked against the current CCA list.
The reference note says Class 3 only is valid for MCA filings. Check the current MCA requirement before buying.
The reference note cites Section 398; confirm that this is the right enabling provision for electronic filing and DSCs.
private: No relief for private companies. The digital signature procedure is the same for every company and LLP that files with the MCA.

title: Incorporating a public company
law: Sections 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 of the Companies Act, 2013; Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014
summary: Sets up a new public limited company through the SPICe+ forms on the MCA portal.
when: When promoters want to form a new public company.
applies: New public companies; minimum 3 directors and 7 subscribers

steps.d: Decide the name and structure and apply for name reservation in SPICe+ Part A. If the name is close to an existing company, get its NOC (by board resolution). If it matches a registered trademark, get the owner's NOC.
docs: NOC from existing company or trademark owner

steps.d: A public company needs at least 3 directors and 7 subscribers. Register their DSCs on the MCA21 version 3 portal.

After name approval, decide authorised and paid-up capital, the registered office, contact details and the directors and subscribers. Prepare DIR-2 consents, the NOC for the registered office and ID and address proofs.
Submit the application with all documents. Collect everything in advance.
The person who signs Part B should also sign AGILE-PRO-S and be available for OTPs.
File e-MOA and e-AOA, or prepare physical copies as the case may be.
Affix DSCs to INC-9 and the other forms and upload to the MCA portal. Pay incorporation fees and stamp duty according to the capital clause of the MOA.
If everything is in order, the Registrar's Central Registration Centre approves the forms and issues the Certificate of Incorporation.
Complete the first auditor appointment, issue share certificates and file INC-20A (commencement of business) within their time limits.
If foreign investment comes in, follow FEMA and RBI rules, including filing FC-GPR.

forms.purpose: PAN, TAN, EPFO, ESIC, GST, bank account and other registrations
Declaration by subscribers and first directors

checklist: Proposed name and any NOC for similar name or trademark
At least 3 directors and 7 subscribers identified
DSCs registered on the MCA portal
ID and address proofs for each director and subscriber
DIR-2 consents
Registered office proof and NOC; utility bill
Capital structure decided
MOA and AOA ready
Fees and stamp duty paid
Plan for first auditor, share certificates and INC-20A

docs.title: NOC from an existing company for a similar name
paras: We, [name of existing company], CIN [CIN], confirm that we have no objection to [proposed name] being used as the name of a new company. This NOC was approved by our Board at its meeting held on [date].
For [name of existing company], [name], Director.

docs.title: NOC from the owner of the registered office
paras: I, [name of owner], owner of the premises at [address], have no objection to the use of these premises as the registered office of {co}. I attach a copy of the utility bill and proof of ownership.
Date: [date]. Signed: [owner].

flags: The reference note does not state time limits for the first auditor, share certificates and INC-20A. By law the first auditor is appointed within 30 days of incorporation (Section 139(6)), share certificates within the time in Section 56, and INC-20A within 180 days of incorporation. Verify.
The reference note does not name e-MOA and e-AOA forms. On the portal these are INC-33 and INC-34.
INC-9 is shown as signed along with the other forms. Check which of SPICe+ Part B, AGILE-PRO-S and INC-9 need separate signatories.
private: None, since this procedure is for incorporating a public company.

title: Converting an LLP into a private limited company
law: Sections 7 and 366 of the Companies Act, 2013; Rules 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 23A, 25, 27, 38 and 38A of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014; Rule 8 of the Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014; Rules 3, 4 and 5 of the Companies (Authorised to Register) Rules, 2014
summary: Registers an existing LLP as a private limited company by filing URC-1 and INC-32 with the Registrar.
when: When the partners of an LLP want to move to a company structure.

steps.d: Get written consent of a majority of partners for registration as a private company.
Publish a notice in Form URC-2 in an English paper and a local-language paper in the LLP's district, inviting objections.

steps.t: Serve the Registrar and get NOC
steps.d: Send a copy of the advertisement to the Registrar and get a NOC from the concerned Registrar.
Apply through RUN with documents and a fee of Rs. 1,000. You can also ask for the name in INC-32, but only if you are confident of availability.
The Central Registration Centre approves or rejects the name. An approved name is valid for 20 days.

Prepare the LLP's statement of accounts, not older than 15 days and certified by an auditor if applicable; NOC from all secured creditors; undertaking from proposed directors on the Stamp Act; declaration that the LLP has filed all documents under the LLP Act; and a statement of pending proceedings.
Prepare the MOA and AOA in Schedule I format. Each subscriber signs in the presence of at least one witness, as Rule 13 requires.

From each resident Indian partner who is a subscriber, get INC-9, a deposits declaration, PAN, ID proof and address proof. For foreign or NRI partners, Indian bodies corporate and foreign bodies corporate, collect the matching sets in the checklist. Foreign documents must be authenticated under Rule 13(5).
From each first director, get INC-9, a deposits declaration, the DIR-2 consent, PAN, ID and address proof. PAN and proofs are not needed if a director already holds an updated DIN.
You may give a temporary correspondence address first. If you give the permanent registered office now, get proof of the address and utility bills not older than 2 months.
Prepare AGILE (INC-35) and the papers for GSTIN, ESIC and EPFO registration.

File with the Registrar's Central Registration Centre, with the fee and the documents listed in the checklist, including lists of partners and proposed directors and, for a guarantee or unlimited company, the guarantee resolution.
docs: CA, CS or CMA Stamp Act certificate

steps.d: If the Registrar finds defects, resubmit within 15 days of the intimation. A second chance of 15 days is allowed. Total time is capped at 30 days.
The Registrar issues the certificate in Form INC-11 with PAN and TAN.

If you gave a temporary address, file INC-22 with proof of the address, utility bills, proof of right to use it if not owned by the company, and photographs showing the exterior, an interior with a director or KMP, and the name board.
For a company with share capital, declare that each subscriber has paid for the shares and that the registered office has been verified. A practising CS, CA or cost accountant verifies it.

forms.purpose: Application to register a company from an LLP
Notice and verification of registered office

checklist: Partners' consent with majority
Newspaper notice and Registrar's NOC
Name approval letter
LLP accounts not older than 15 days
NOC from all secured creditors
Stamp Act undertaking and certificate
LLP Act filings declaration
Statement of pending proceedings
Signed MOA and AOA with witness
INC-9 and deposit declarations from partners and directors
DIR-2 consents with PAN and ID proofs
Registered office proof, utility bills, NOC
Certificate of the LLP and latest tax return
Lists of partners and proposed directors

docs.title: Consent of partners to conversion
paras: We, the undersigned partners of [name of LLP], LLPIN [LLPIN], being a majority of the partners, consent to the registration of the LLP as a private limited company under Section 366 of the Companies Act, 2013, under the name {co}.
We authorise [name of partner] to publish the notice in Form URC-2, apply for the name and sign all documents. Signed: [names of partners]. Date: [date].

docs.title: Undertaking by proposed directors on stamp duty
paras: We, the proposed directors of {co}, undertake to comply with the requirements of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 in relation to the conversion of [name of LLP] into a company.
Signed: [names of directors]. Date: [date].

docs.title: Board resolution of a corporate partner to subscribe to the MOA
paras: RESOLVED THAT [name of body corporate] subscribes to the Memorandum of Association of {co} for [number] shares and [name of representative] is authorised to sign the MOA, INC-9 and related papers on its behalf.

flags: The reference note gives name approval validity as 20 days and does not mention extension. Check the current rule; other procedures in the same set speak of extension.

The reference note mentions both Registrar's NOC and the Registrar being served the copy of the advertisement; the NOC from the LLP's Registrar is the key document. Verify how the NOC is requested on the portal.
The reference note says documents from non-residents must be authenticated under Rule 13(5). Confirm the mode (apostille, notary, embassy) applicable to each country.

title: Converting a private company into a public company
law: Sections 2(68), 2(71), 13, 14 and 18; Rule 33 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014
summary: Changes a private company into a public company by altering the articles and name, and filing INC-27.
when: When a private company wants to become public, for example to raise funds from the public or list.

steps.d: Send notice at least 7 days before. Approve the conversion, the alteration of AOA to remove the private company restrictions in Section 2(68), the EGM notice, and the change of name to drop the word Private.
Pass a special resolution for conversion, alteration of AOA and MOA and the change of name. A special resolution needs at least 75% of the members present and voting.
File the special resolution with its attachments.
Apply for conversion with the altered MOA and AOA, the special resolution, EGM minutes, list of members, directors' declaration and the board resolution.
If the name change needs it, file INC-24 to drop the word Private, with the resolution, altered MOA and AOA and any Central Government consent.
After verification the Registrar issues a fresh certificate of incorporation showing public company status and the portal is updated.

Update PAN, TAN, GST, bank and other records. Change nameplate, letterhead and invoices. Meet the minimum numbers of directors and members. Appoint KMP where required by paid-up capital. If you plan to list, SEBI and listing rules apply as well.

forms.deadline: As the reference note says, if required

checklist: Board resolution approving conversion
Special resolution passed at the EGM
Altered AOA without private company restrictions
Altered MOA with new name and status
List of members
Directors' declaration
At least 3 directors and 7 members in place
EGM minutes
PAN, TAN, GST, bank and other records updated
Letterhead, nameplate and invoices changed

meetings.title: Board meeting to approve conversion
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter if the Act and Secretarial Standard 1 allow)

meetings.title: EGM to approve the conversion
meetings.notice_days: At least 21 clear days (shorter if members holding at least 95% of voting power agree)

resolutions.title: Approval of conversion and EGM notice
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, subject to the approval of the members, {co} be converted from a private company into a public company under Section 18 of the Companies Act, 2013, and its name be changed to [new name] Limited. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Memorandum and Articles of Association be altered as placed before the meeting, to remove the provisions that make the company a private company under Section 2(68). RESOLVED FURTHER THAT an Extraordinary General Meeting be held on [date] at [time] at [venue], the notice with explanatory statement be approved, and [name of director / company secretary] is authorised to issue it and make all filings.

resolutions.title: Conversion into a public company
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, under Sections 13, 14 and 18 of the Companies Act, 2013 and Rule 33 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014, {co} be converted into a public company and the word Private be deleted from its name, so that it is called [new name] Limited. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Memorandum of Association be altered in the name and other clauses, and the Articles of Association be altered by removing the provisions required for a private company, as placed before the meeting. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director] is authorised to file the necessary forms.
resolutions.explanatory: The company proposes to become a public company because [reason]. The alterations are: name clause, status clause of the MOA and the private company restrictions in the AOA. The Board recommends the special resolution. No director or key managerial personnel is interested except as a member, if at all.

flags: The reference note says conversion needs a special resolution only. In the Act, a conversion from public to private needs Regional Director approval under the proviso to Section 14(1). Private to public does not. Verify before telling the client that consent is needed.

The reference note asks to file INC-24 for the name change. When the only change is dropping the word Private, no Registrar approval is needed under Section 13(2); the name change is usually handled inside INC-27. Check the current portal practice.
The time limit for INC-27 is not in the reference note. Check the rule; filing within 30 days of the special resolution is the practice I know.
The reference note puts Board notice at 7 days and special resolution at 75% of members present and voting. Both match the law for ordinary cases.

title: Converting a private company into a One Person Company
law: Section 18 of the Companies Act, 2013; Rule 7 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014; Rule 3 of the same Rules (eligibility)
summary: Turns a private company with a single member into a One Person Company after consents from members and creditors.
when: When a private company is left with one individual owner who wants an OPC.
applies: Private companies; sole member must be a natural person who is an Indian citizen

steps.d: The shareholder must not be a member of another OPC. Only a natural person who is an Indian citizen, in India or abroad, can be member and nominee of an OPC. The reference note says no capital or turnover limit applies after the 2021 amendment.
Give notice at least 7 days before. Take in-principle approval, fix the date, time and day of the EGM, approve the draft EGM notice and authorise a director to send it.
Before the EGM, collect written no-objection from existing shareholders and creditors to the conversion.
Send the notice to members, directors and auditors at least 21 days before the meeting, or as the AOA says.

Check quorum throughout and that the auditor attends, or has leave of absence under Section 146. Pass a special resolution to convert into an OPC and another special resolution to alter the MOA and AOA.
File the special resolution.
File Form INC-26 (as the reference note names it) with the NOCs and other documents. The reference note says the form must be published at least 14 days before the Regional Director's hearing.
After the Registrar is satisfied, the office issues a fresh certificate of incorporation.

forms.purpose: Application (as named in the reference note)

checklist: Sole member is an Indian citizen, a natural person and not a member of another OPC
Nominee identified with consent
Board resolution
Written NOCs from shareholders and creditors
EGM notice sent 21 days before
Special resolutions passed
Auditor present or leave of absence noted
MGT-14 filed
Altered MOA and AOA

meetings.title: Board meeting to approve conversion
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter if the Act and Secretarial Standard 1 allow)

meetings.title: EGM to approve conversion into OPC
meetings.notice_days: At least 21 clear days (shorter if members holding at least 95% of voting power agree)

resolutions.title: Approval of conversion into OPC and EGM notice
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, subject to the approval of the member, the company be converted into a One Person Company under Section 18 of the Companies Act, 2013 and Rule 7 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014, with the name changed to [new name] (OPC) Private Limited. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT an Extraordinary General Meeting be held on [date] at [time] at [venue] and the draft notice be approved. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director] is authorised to issue the notice and make filings.

resolutions.title: Conversion into a One Person Company
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, under Section 18 of the Companies Act, 2013 and Rule 7 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014, {co} be converted into a One Person Company, and [name] be the nominee of the sole member. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director] is authorised to file the applications and do all things needed.
resolutions.explanatory: The company has a single member, [name], who has asked that it be converted into an OPC. All shareholders and creditors have given their no-objection. [Add details.] The Board recommends the special resolution. No director is interested except [name], to the extent of the shareholding.

resolutions.title: Alteration of MOA and AOA for an OPC
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, under Sections 13 and 14 of the Companies Act, 2013, the Memorandum and Articles of Association be altered as placed before the meeting, to suit a One Person Company, and the name clause be changed to [new name] (OPC) Private Limited.
resolutions.explanatory: The existing documents refer to several members. The changes cover [clauses] and the name clause as shown in the draft placed before the meeting.

docs.title: NOC from a creditor
paras: We, [name of creditor], creditor of {co}, have no objection to its conversion into a One Person Company. Amount outstanding: Rs. [amount in Rs.]. Date: [date]. Signed: [name], [designation].

flags: The reference note says the application form is INC-26. I believe INC-26 is the form for shifting the registered office between states; conversion to OPC under Rule 7 is filed in Form INC-6 with the Registrar. Verify the form.
The reference note says the special resolution needs three-fourths of total shareholding. The law requires at least three times as many votes in favour as against, not total shareholding.
The reference note says the member must be resident for 'one hundred and twenty eighty-two days'. The garbled text should read 120 days after the 2021 amendment (it was 182 days earlier). Verify.
The company must first reduce to one member. The reference note does not describe how; transfer or buy-back is needed before the EGM.
The reference note says board notice goes to 'all members'. Board notices go to directors.
The OPC's name must carry (OPC) in brackets below the name; not in the reference note.

extras.h: What the company must meet to become an OPC (Rule 3)
items: The sole member must not be a member of any other OPC.
Only a natural person who is an Indian citizen, resident in India or not, can be the member and the nominee of an OPC.
'Resident in India' means staying in India for at least 120 days in the previous financial year (182 days under the earlier rule, so check the current text).
After the Registrar is satisfied, his office issues a fresh certificate of incorporation, which completes the conversion.

title: Altering the Memorandum of Association
law: Sections 4, 13, 15, 12 and 61 of the Companies Act, 2013; Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014
summary: Changes the name, state of registered office, objects, liability or capital clause of the MOA by general meeting approval and filings.
when: When the company needs to change any clause of its MOA.
applies: All companies; extra approvals for Section 8 and regulated companies

steps.d: Give notice under Section 173 and SS-1.
steps.time: At least 7 days (or shorter if allowed)

steps.d: Approve the alteration of the clause (name, state, objects, liability or capital), authorise directors or KMP to sign documents, approve the general meeting notice and appoint a scrutiniser if needed. A Section 8 company must first get the Registrar's permission. A company with a sector regulator (IRDA, RBI, SEBI) needs in-principle approval first. For capital changes, check the AOA gives the power. The MOA must follow Table A to E of Schedule I.

steps.t: File RUN for a name change
steps.d: Check name availability with the Central Registration Centre. A name approved through RUN is valid for 60 days, so get shareholder approval within it.
Send the general meeting notice under Section 101 and SS-2 with the Section 102 explanatory statement.
steps.time: At least 21 days (or shorter if allowed)

steps.d: Pass a special resolution for any clause under Section 13, except an ordinary resolution under Section 61 for the capital clause.
File with the attachments listed in the checklist.

File INC-24 (name), INC-22 (registered office) or SH-7 (capital) as needed, with the resolution, altered MOA and AOA, optional minutes, attendance sheets and scrutiniser report, proof of address and photographs for an address change.
Mention the alteration in the Board report and the annual return of the year it occurs. Post it on the website, if any, and rename the website if the name changes.

A name change takes effect on the Registrar's written approval, but no approval is needed if only the word Private is added or dropped due to conversion. A change of registered office to another state takes effect on Central Government approval. Any other alteration takes effect only when the Registrar registers it.

Note the alteration in every copy of the MOA. Update the seal if required by the AOA, stationery, stamps, sign boards, statutory registers, share certificates, bank and demat accounts, and tax and other registrations.

forms.purpose: Notice of alteration of share capital

checklist: Clause to be changed identified
Prior permission of Registrar (Section 8) or regulator approval, if applicable
Authority in the AOA for capital change
RUN approval for a name change and NOC from similar-name company or trademark owner
Board resolution
Notice and explanatory statement sent
Resolutions passed; scrutiniser's report
Certified true copy of resolution
Altered MOA and AOA; subscription sheet
Address proof and photographs for an address change
MGT-14, INC-34 and clause-specific forms filed
Registers, website and stationery updated

meetings.title: Board meeting to approve alteration of MOA
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter if the Act and Secretarial Standard 1 allow)

meetings.title: General meeting to alter the MOA
meetings.notice_days: At least 21 clear days (shorter if members holding at least 95% of voting power agree)

resolutions.title: Approval of alteration of MOA and notice
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT the alteration of the [name / registered office / objects / liability / capital] clause of the Memorandum of Association of {co}, as placed before the meeting, be approved, subject to the approval of the members. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the notice of the general meeting to be held on [date] at [time] at [venue], with explanatory statement under Section 102, be approved, and [name of scrutiniser] be appointed as scrutiniser. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [names of directors / KMP] are authorised to sign all documents, file forms and obtain approvals.

resolutions.title: Alteration of a clause of the MOA (not capital)
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, under Section 13 of the Companies Act, 2013 and the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014, the [name / objects / liability / situation of registered office] clause of the Memorandum of Association be altered as follows: [text of altered clause]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director / company secretary] is authorised to file Forms MGT-14, INC-34 and [INC-24 / INC-22] and do all things needed.
resolutions.explanatory: The company proposes to alter its Memorandum. The reason is [reason]. The existing clause reads [existing clause]; the proposed clause reads [proposed clause]. [Any required approval: Registrar, regulator, NOC.] The Board recommends the special resolution. No director or key managerial personnel is interested except as a member, if at all.

resolutions.title: Alteration of the capital clause of the MOA
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, under Section 61 and Section 13 of the Companies Act, 2013 and as permitted by the Articles of Association, the capital clause of the Memorandum be altered so that the authorised share capital be Rs. [amount in Rs.] divided into [number] equity shares of Rs. [face value] each. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director / company secretary] is authorised to file Forms SH-7 and MGT-14.
resolutions.explanatory: The authorised capital is being altered to [reason]. The Board recommends the ordinary resolution. No director is interested except to the extent of any shares held.

flags: The reference note says change of state of registered office needs Central Government approval but does not describe the Regional Director filing (INC-23) or INC-28. Verify the full route.
The reference note gives the name validity as 60 days for RUN; other procedures say 20 days for new companies. Check the portal.
The reference note lists the filing of 'MGT INC 24, INC 22, SH 7' with a garbled label. Read as INC-24, INC-22 and SH-7 as the case may be.
Change of objects may carry extra duties if the company raised money by a prospectus (Section 13(8)). The reference note does not mention this.

title: Altering the Articles of Association
law: Section 14 of the Companies Act, 2013; Rule 33 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014; Sections 6 and 10; shareholders' and joint venture agreements
summary: Changes the articles by special resolution, usually to reflect a shareholders' or joint venture agreement or a change in law or class of company.
when: When the rules of the company need to change, for example to add investor rights or move to Table F.
applies: All companies; a private company may use shorter notice if its articles allow

steps.d: Discuss the changes needed, draft the altered AOA and confirm that nothing breaks the Act or other laws. If there is foreign investment, check FEMA and RBI rules. If listed, check SEBI LODR and get exchange approval if needed.
docs: Marked-up comparison of old and new

steps.d: Give 7 days' notice, unless shorter notice is agreed (Section 173, SS-1). Consider and recommend the draft AOA, fix the EGM date, time and venue, approve the notice and explanatory statement, and authorise a director or company secretary to send the notice and file forms.
Send to members, directors and auditors at least 21 clear days before, or shorter if the AOA allows. State the text of the alteration, the reason and that it is a special resolution.
Check quorum under Section 103, pass the special resolution and keep minutes under Section 118 and SS-2.

File MGT-14 with the linked INC-34 (e-AOA). Attach the certified special resolution, EGM notice with explanatory statement, altered AOA (marked or complete) and the board resolution authorising the filing. Pay the fee based on authorised capital.
Update every copy of the AOA and circulate it to directors, auditors and others. If listed, inform the exchanges. Check that agreements such as SHA or JV agreement still match.

If the alteration adds or removes entrenchment provisions, the reference note also asks for INC-27. A move from private to public or the reverse needs INC-27. Foreign-investment companies may need RBI approval for share rights changes.

forms.purpose: Conversion or entrenchment filing (as stated in the reference note)

checklist: Draft altered AOA and marked-up comparison
Legal opinion if the change is significant
Board notice and resolution
EGM notice with Section 102 statement
Special resolution passed (75% of votes cast)
Minutes under SS-2
MGT-14 with INC-34 filed
Certified resolution and altered AOA attached
Stock exchange approval or intimation if listed
FEMA or RBI check if foreign investment
Shareholders' agreement terms reflected in the AOA

meetings.title: Board meeting to approve alteration of AOA
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter if the Act and Secretarial Standard 1 allow)

meetings.title: EGM to alter the AOA
meetings.notice_days: At least 21 clear days (shorter if members holding at least 95% of voting power agree)

resolutions.title: Approval of alteration of AOA and EGM notice
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT the alteration of the Articles of Association of {co}, as set out in the draft placed before the meeting, be approved and recommended to the members under Section 14 of the Companies Act, 2013. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT an Extraordinary General Meeting be held on [date] at [time] at [venue] and the notice with the explanatory statement under Section 102 be approved. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director / company secretary] is authorised to issue the notice and file all forms.

resolutions.title: Alteration of the Articles of Association
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, under Section 14 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and Rule 33 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014, the Articles of Association of {co} be altered by [inserting / deleting / substituting] [clause numbers] as set out in the draft placed before the meeting [or: be replaced by a new set of Articles]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director / company secretary] is authorised to file Form MGT-14 and the linked forms and do all things needed.
resolutions.explanatory: The proposed alteration is needed because [reason, such as the shareholders' agreement dated (date)]. The changes are: [summary of changes]. A comparison of the old and new articles is available for inspection at the registered office. The Board recommends the special resolution. No director or key managerial personnel is interested except [name], to the extent of [interest].

flags: The reference note says a private-to-public conversion needs Central Government (Regional Director) approval under Section 14(1). The proviso covers the opposite direction, public to private. Verify.
The reference note asks for INC-27 for entrenchment provisions. INC-27 is the conversion form; entrenchment (Section 5(5) and (6)) is, as far as I know, notified with MGT-14. Verify.
Section 14(2) also requires filing the altered articles within 15 days; check against the 30-day MGT-14 period in the reference note.
